title: Cooperation dynamics between persuasion-prone and persuasion-averse populations under random sequential guidance
summary: Social guidance, as a universal mechanism to promote collective cooperation, effectively maintains and enhances the level of population cooperation by correcting the behavior of defectors. However, existing guidance models have two key limitations: first, they assume that guidance actions are inevitably successful; second, they neglect information sharing among guides, leading to repeated guidance of the same successfully guided defector.
